title: SailPoint Admin Domain 8 questions (8.1)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with SailPoint.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST defines identity governance and administration (IGA)?
choices: Encrypting sensitive data at rest on every server and database in the company
Blocking malicious network traffic at the perimeter
Managing who has access to what and proving that access is appropriate
Signing users in to every application with one password and a second factor
questions.answer: Managing who has access to what and proving that access is appropriate
questions.explanation: IGA covers the identity lifecycle, provisioning, requests, reviews and policy, with evidence for auditors. Single sign-on is access management, which controls the sign-in itself.

questions.stem: A company already has SSO and MFA, but auditors ask for evidence of why each user was given access to the finance app. Which capability is missing?
choices: A stronger second factor for signing in to the finance application
A faster identity provider that can handle more sign-ins at peak times
A web application firewall
Identity governance with request, approval and review records
questions.answer: Identity governance with request, approval and review records
questions.explanation: SSO and MFA prove who signed in but not why access was granted. IGA records approvals and reviews that answer the auditor's question.

questions.stem: In an IGA program, what is an authoritative source?
choices: Any application that has user accounts
The directory that stores the most user passwords and service accounts
The ticketing system that stores all access requests and approvals
The trusted system, such as HR, that defines who an identity is
questions.answer: The trusted system, such as HR, that defines who an identity is
questions.explanation: An authoritative source supplies the trusted identity data that drives the lifecycle. Other applications hold accounts that are correlated to those identities.

questions.stem: How is an identity related to accounts in identity governance?
choices: Each account is a separate identity
One identity can own many accounts across different systems
An identity can own only one account, on its authoritative source
Accounts exist only in the authoritative source and nowhere else
questions.answer: One identity can own many accounts across different systems
questions.explanation: An identity represents the person, and their accounts on each system are linked to it. Treating each account as its own identity hides the full picture of access.

questions.stem: An auditor asks what an entitlement is in governance terms. What is the BEST answer?
choices: The person's job title and cost center as recorded in the HR system
A specific permission or group on a system that grants some access
A password policy applied to all users
The total number of accounts a person owns across all connected systems
questions.answer: A specific permission or group on a system that grants some access
questions.explanation: Entitlements are the fine-grained rights, such as groups or permissions, that accounts hold. Job titles are identity attributes that may drive access.

questions.stem: A review finds active accounts on several systems that belong to no current identity. What are these called?
choices: Birthright accounts
Orphaned accounts
Service identities
Authoritative accounts
questions.answer: Orphaned accounts
questions.explanation: Orphaned accounts have no valid owner, often because a leaver was not deprovisioned. They are a common audit finding and attack path.

questions.stem: What is a key benefit of grouping entitlements into roles based on job function?
choices: Every user gets every entitlement, so requests are never needed
Access is granted consistently and reviewed at a business level
Passwords no longer need to be changed
Reviews are no longer needed for any access
questions.answer: Access is granted consistently and reviewed at a business level
questions.explanation: Roles bundle the access a job needs so it is assigned the same way each time and is easier to understand. Roles still need review.

questions.stem: A new employee needs email, the intranet and the timesheet app on day one without filing requests. What IGA concept provides this?
choices: Birthright access granted at the joiner event
Access granted only after the next quarterly review
Access requested by the new hire through the portal on day one
Access copied from a coworker's account
questions.answer: Birthright access granted at the joiner event
questions.explanation: Birthright access is assigned automatically when a joiner appears in the authoritative source. Copying a coworker's access spreads excess rights.

questions.stem: An analyst moved from Finance to Marketing and still has Finance system access months later. What problem does this show?
choices: Privilege creep from a mover process that kept old access
A leaver process that ran too early and removed the wrong access
A joiner process that granted too little access on day one
A strong password policy that failed
questions.answer: Privilege creep from a mover process that kept old access
questions.explanation: Movers should lose access they no longer need. When old access stays, rights build up over time, which is privilege creep.

questions.stem: An employee is terminated today. What should the leaver process do with their access?
choices: Leave it in place until the next quarterly access review revokes it
Transfer it to the employee's manager
Disable or remove it promptly across all connected systems
Keep it active for a few months in case the employee is rehired
questions.answer: Disable or remove it promptly across all connected systems
questions.explanation: Prompt deprovisioning prevents a former employee from using access after leaving. Waiting for a review leaves a dangerous gap.

questions.stem: What usually starts joiner, mover and leaver processes in an automated IGA program?
choices: Requests typed by each user
Random audits of each department's user list
Password expiry on the directory
Changes to identity data from the authoritative source
questions.answer: Changes to identity data from the authoritative source
questions.explanation: Hires, transfers and terminations recorded in HR flow in as attribute changes that drive lifecycle actions. Relying on users to ask leads to missed changes.

questions.stem: Contractors are engaged for fixed terms. What is the BEST way to make sure their access stops when the term finishes?
choices: Use their end date to drive automatic removal of access
Ask each contractor to report to the help desk when they leave
Remove access only during annual reviews
Give contractors shared accounts that are removed at project close
questions.answer: Use their end date to drive automatic removal of access
questions.explanation: Driving removal from a known end date closes access without depending on someone to remember. Shared accounts break accountability.

questions.stem: A former employee is rehired after a year. What should a well-governed process do?
choices: Restore every account and entitlement exactly as it was before
Give them administrator rights to save time
Grant fresh access for the new role instead of restoring it
Skip provisioning until they ask for access
questions.answer: Grant fresh access for the new role instead of restoring it
questions.explanation: A returning employee may have a different job, so access should match the new role. Restoring everything can reintroduce rights no longer needed.

questions.stem: Why is automating the leaver process a strong compliance control?
choices: It removes access consistently and records when it happened
It lets terminated users keep email and file access for a year
It removes the need for any authoritative source
It prevents new employees from being hired
questions.answer: It removes access consistently and records when it happened
questions.explanation: Automated deprovisioning is timely and repeatable and produces evidence for auditors. Manual steps are easy to miss.

questions.stem: Which regulation MOST directly drives access controls over systems used for public company financial reporting in the US?
choices: HIPAA
Sarbanes-Oxley Act
GDPR
FERPA
questions.answer: Sarbanes-Oxley Act
questions.explanation: SOX requires internal controls over financial reporting, which include who can access and change financial systems. HIPAA covers health information.

questions.stem: A hospital must restrict and review access to patient health records. Which regulation is the main driver?
choices: Sarbanes-Oxley Act
PCI DSS
GLBA
HIPAA
questions.answer: HIPAA
questions.explanation: HIPAA protects health information and expects access to it to be limited and monitored. PCI DSS covers payment card data.

questions.stem: A retailer stores and processes payment card numbers. Which standard requires access to that data to be limited by need to know?
choices: HIPAA
GDPR
PCI DSS
FISMA
questions.answer: PCI DSS
questions.explanation: PCI DSS sets requirements for protecting cardholder data, including restricting access by business need. GDPR covers personal data more broadly.

questions.stem: A company processes personal data of people in the European Union. Which regulation shapes its access and data-minimisation duties?
choices: Sarbanes-Oxley Act
GDPR
HIPAA
PCI DSS
questions.answer: GDPR
questions.explanation: GDPR governs personal data of people in the EU and expects access to be limited and accountable. SOX is about financial reporting controls.

questions.stem: In identity governance, what does compliance mean?
choices: Meeting regulations and internal policies, and proving it
Buying the newest security tools each year
Granting whatever access users request if their manager is told
Passing a single audit once and stopping
questions.answer: Meeting regulations and internal policies, and proving it
questions.explanation: Compliance is meeting the required rules and showing evidence that you do. A one-off pass without ongoing controls is not sustained compliance.

questions.stem: Which is an example of a preventive identity control?
choices: Reviewing last quarter's access in a campaign and revoking errors
Reading audit logs after an incident
Blocking an access request that would create an SoD conflict
Reporting orphaned accounts each month
questions.answer: Blocking an access request that would create an SoD conflict
questions.explanation: Preventive controls stop a problem before it happens. Certifications and reports are detective controls that find problems afterward.

questions.stem: An organisation wants to show compliance continuously rather than scrambling before each audit. What approach BEST supports this?
choices: Automated policies, reviews and reports all year
One large manual review in the week before the audit
Temporary admin rights for the auditors
Deleting old logs to reduce what auditors see
questions.answer: Automated policies, reviews and reports all year
questions.explanation: Ongoing automated controls keep access in line and produce evidence at any time. A last-minute review is point-in-time and easy to fail.

questions.topic: Least Privilege and Separation of Duties
questions.stem: Which statement BEST describes the principle of least privilege?
choices: Users get the same access as their manager
Users get broad access to avoid delays
Users get broad access, which is reduced only after an incident
Users get only the access needed for their job, for as long as they need it
questions.answer: Users get only the access needed for their job, for as long as they need it
questions.explanation: Least privilege limits access to what the job requires, reducing the damage if an account is misused. Copying a manager's access usually grants too much.

questions.topic: Least Privilege and Separation of Duties
questions.stem: A single user can both create a new vendor and approve payments to that vendor. What control is missing?
choices: Single sign-on
Separation of duties
Birthright access
Data encryption
questions.answer: Separation of duties
questions.explanation: Separation of duties splits conflicting tasks so one person cannot commit and hide fraud. SSO only affects how users sign in.

questions.topic: Least Privilege and Separation of Duties
questions.stem: What is a toxic combination in access governance?
choices: An enabled account whose password has expired on several systems
Two or more rights that together let one person misuse a process
A role that has no entitlements
A source with no owner assigned
questions.answer: Two or more rights that together let one person misuse a process
questions.explanation: A toxic combination is access that is acceptable alone but risky together, such as create and approve. SoD policies define and detect them.

questions.topic: Least Privilege and Separation of Duties
questions.stem: A rare business need requires one user to hold two conflicting entitlements for a week. What is the BEST governance response?
choices: Grant both entitlements permanently and keep no record of it
Approve a time-limited, documented exception with mitigation
Deny all access to both systems
Remove the separation of duties policy
questions.answer: Approve a time-limited, documented exception with mitigation
questions.explanation: A documented exception with an end date and compensating checks keeps the risk visible and limited. Removing the policy hides all future conflicts.

questions.topic: Least Privilege and Separation of Duties
questions.stem: Why are privileged accounts usually reviewed more often than standard user access?
choices: Privileged accounts are never used
Privileged users dislike reviews
Misuse of privileged access causes much greater impact
Standard accounts cannot be included in certifications
questions.answer: Misuse of privileged access causes much greater impact
questions.explanation: Higher-risk access deserves more frequent review because the damage from misuse is higher. Review frequency should follow risk.

questions.topic: Least Privilege and Separation of Duties
questions.stem: A developer needs production database access for a two-day incident. Which approach BEST follows least privilege?
choices: Grant permanent access so the developer is ready for future incidents
Share the database admin's credentials
Add the developer to every admin group
Grant time-bound access that is removed when the need ends
questions.answer: Grant time-bound access that is removed when the need ends
questions.explanation: Time-bound access gives what is needed only while needed. Permanent grants and shared credentials leave standing risk.

questions.topic: Least Privilege and Separation of Duties
questions.stem: Where should a separation of duties check run to prevent a conflict rather than only detect it?
choices: Only in the yearly external audit
Only after the user leaves and the accounts are closed
When access is requested, before it is provisioned
Only when passwords are reset
questions.answer: When access is requested, before it is provisioned
questions.explanation: Checking at request time stops the conflict before access is granted. Audits and later reviews find conflicts that already exist.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of an access certification?
choices: To provision new accounts for joiners based on their job title
To reset passwords for locked users
To create new sources in the tenant
To have reviewers confirm or revoke existing access regularly
questions.answer: To have reviewers confirm or revoke existing access regularly
questions.explanation: Certifications are periodic reviews where a reviewer decides whether access is still appropriate. Provisioning and password resets are separate processes.

questions.stem: Managers approve every item in their reviews within seconds without reading them. What is this problem called?
choices: Rubber-stamping
Privilege escalation
Correlation
Birthright provisioning
questions.answer: Rubber-stamping
questions.explanation: Rubber-stamping means approving without real review, which makes certifications worthless as a control. Smaller, focused reviews with context help.

questions.stem: Which evidence from an access review is MOST useful to an auditor?
choices: The number of reminder emails sent to reviewers and opened
A screenshot of the review dashboard
Who reviewed each item, the decision, when, and proof revoked access was removed
The reviewers' job titles only
questions.answer: Who reviewed each item, the decision, when, and proof revoked access was removed
questions.explanation: Auditors need decisions, accountability, timing and remediation proof. Email counts and screenshots do not show that access was actually controlled.

questions.stem: A reviewer revokes an entitlement in a certification. What makes this a closed-loop process?
choices: The revocation is provisioned to the system and its completion is recorded
The reviewer emails the app owner and nobody follows up
The decision is saved but never acted on
The entitlement is removed only from the report
questions.answer: The revocation is provisioned to the system and its completion is recorded
questions.explanation: Closed-loop remediation carries the decision through to the target system and confirms it. A saved decision with no removal leaves the access in place.

questions.stem: A team must decide how often to review access to different applications. What is the BEST basis?
choices: The alphabetical order of the applications in the source list
How many users complain about reviews
The risk and sensitivity of each application's access
A single yearly date for every system
questions.answer: The risk and sensitivity of each application's access
questions.explanation: Risk-based scheduling reviews sensitive access more often and low-risk access less. One date for everything over-reviews some and under-reviews others.

questions.stem: A certification lists highly technical database entitlements. Which reviewer is MOST likely to make informed decisions about them?
choices: The application or entitlement owner who understands the access
A random employee from another department, chosen for impartiality
The newest hire in the company
The user who holds the access
questions.answer: The application or entitlement owner who understands the access
questions.explanation: Owners understand what technical entitlements allow, so their decisions are more accurate. Users reviewing their own access is a conflict of interest.

questions.stem: Why does an IGA platform keep an audit trail of access requests, approvals and changes?
choices: To make aggregations run faster
To replace approvals, since every change is logged afterwards
To store user passwords for recovery
To show what happened, who did it and when during audits and investigations
questions.answer: To show what happened, who did it and when during audits and investigations
questions.explanation: An audit trail is evidence of decisions and changes. It supports audits and investigations and does not replace controls.

questions.stem: Put the steps of an automated leaver process in order, starting from HR.
items: HR records the termination in the authoritative source
The next aggregation updates the identity's attributes
The identity moves to a terminated lifecycle state
Accounts are disabled and access is removed on connected systems
The results are recorded for audit evidence
questions.explanation: The authoritative source drives the change, the lifecycle state applies the leaver policy and provisioning removes access. The recorded results become evidence.

questions.stem: Match each regulation or standard to its main focus.

pairs.match: Controls over public company financial reporting
Personal data of people in the European Union

questions.explanation: Each regulation targets a type of data or process that access governance must protect. Wireless encryption is a technical standard, not one of these regulations.

questions.topic: Least Privilege and Separation of Duties
questions.stem: An organisation wants to PREVENT separation of duties violations, not only find them later. Which TWO controls help?
choices: Check SoD policies when access is requested
Design roles so conflicting rights are not bundled together
Run a yearly certification of all access
Report conflicts after each external audit
Read the audit log after an incident
answers: Check SoD policies when access is requested
Design roles so conflicting rights are not bundled together
questions.explanation: Request-time checks and careful role design stop conflicts before access is granted. Certifications, reports and log reviews are detective controls.
